# Lixiana

Lixiana is a direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC) named in the AFDK (Atrieflimren i Danmark) quality program documentation as one of several branded anticoagulant medicines whose patient information materials are recommended for use in structured patient education about atrial fibrillation [^src1]. It is mentioned once in the corpus, alongside Xarelto, Eliquis, and Pradaxa, as part of a set of pharmaceutical company pamphlets ("pjecer") that, together with regional pamphlets on AK (anticoagulant) treatment, are made available to patients [^src1].

The mention appears in the chapter documenting Indicator 8 (Struktureret patientuddannelse) of the AFDK program, which is administered by Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram. That chapter presents the evidence base for patient education as an integrated part of atrial fibrillation treatment, drawing on European ESC guidelines and Danish national guidelines, and describes the purpose, methods, content, and implementation of structured patient education, including the ABC Pathway model of integrated atrial fibrillation care — covering stroke prevention (A), better symptom control (B), and cardiovascular risk reduction (C) [^src1]. No further details about Lixiana itself — such as its manufacturer, dosage, or clinical trial data — are given in this corpus.
